about: Hardware inputs of the simulation: one entry per number, grouped by device, plus the mission numbers (orbit, start date). Bench results go here.
Each entry: value (null = unknown, not applied), units (fixed per entry; convert the number, not the units),
source (assumed | datasheet | measured), note (where the number comes from, or which bench test replaces it).
Checked by scalar/hardware.py. Used by the as-built rows (python3 scripts/matrix.py --experiments hw) and by
scripts/gyro_realism.py, mag_realism.py, sun_realism.py. The reference runs (experiments 1-6, --gate) never read it.
After editing: python3 -m pytest tests/test_hardware.py -q, then rerun the as-built rows, then python3 scripts/report.py --write.
Hardware numbers that are not in this file, where they live and why: docs/LIMITATIONS.md, part "Inputs not in hardware.json".

noise_density.note: Rate noise density (angle random walk). scalar/sensors/gyro.py lines 12 and 62 call it a representative published LSM6DSO figure; not checked against the datasheet. Replaced by the Allan deviation of the 2 h static log (verification-loop plan, phase 5).

bias_random_walk.note: Rate random walk of the bias, scalar/sensors/gyro.py line 79; no source given. Replaced by the Allan deviation of the 2 h static log (phase 5).

initial_bias.note: Zero-rate output per axis at the start of a run, scalar/sensors/gyro.py line 80; no source given. Replaced by the mean of the 2 h static log (phase 5).

scale_factor.note: Scale-factor error per axis (0.01 = reads 1 % high). Size 1 % from docs/verification-loop-plan.md row 1h; same sign on all axes is a choice (was ASSUMED_SCALE_FACTOR_SIGNS in scripts/gyro_realism.py). Replaced by a rate-table run of the flight board, each axis both directions.

misalignment.note: Rotation vector of the sensor axes from the body axes (v_sensor = C v_body). 0.5 deg from docs/verification-loop-plan.md row 1h, about the body diagonal (1, 1, 1)/sqrt(3), a choice (was ASSUMED_MISALIGN_AXIS in scripts/gyro_realism.py). Replaced by the same rate-table run (cross-axis response).

lsb.note: Output step. The author's recollection of the LSM6DSO step at +-250 deg/s, not checked against the datasheet or the flight code (scripts/gyro_realism.py, was ASSUMED_GYRO_LSB_DEG_S). Replaced by the range the flight driver sets and the step seen in the 2 h static log.

temp_coeff.note: Zero-rate drift per kelvin, per axis. Size from the author's recollection, signs a choice (scripts/gyro_realism.py, was ASSUMED_GYRO_TEMP_COEFF_DEG_S_PER_K). Replaced by the phase-5 temperature ramp with the TMP112s: slope of each axis' static output against temperature.

noise_std.note: White noise per axis, 1 sigma. scalar/sensors/magnetometer.py lines 42 and 61 call it a representative published LIS2MDL figure; not checked against the datasheet. Replaced by the 2 h static log (phase 5).

hard_iron_bias.note: Offset in body axes, the plant of the notes, section 6 (scalar/control/rl_tune.py line 75). Replaced by the ellipsoid fit of the board rotated through all orientations (phase 5).

soft_iron.note: Distortion matrix D (B_meas = D B + b), the plant of the notes, section 6 (scalar/control/rl_tune.py lines 76-77). Replaced by the same ellipsoid fit (phase 5).

lsb.note: Output step, 0.15 uT from docs/verification-loop-plan.md row 1c (scalar/sensors/magnetometer.py line 64). Replaced by the step seen in the 2 h static log.

temp_coeff.note: Offset drift per kelvin, per axis; no file states it (scripts/mag_realism.py, was ASSUMED_TEMP_COEFF_T_PER_K). Replaced by the phase-5 temperature ramp with the TMP112s: slope of each axis' offset against temperature.

integration_time.note: VEML6031 integration time; one of 400, 200, 100, 50, 25, 12.5, 6.25. The module default (scalar/sensors/veml6031.py line 72), which tests/test_veml6031.py calls the flight setting; at 25 ms the sensor clips in direct sun (notes, section 12). Replaced by the rotary-stage test: the setting that survives full sun (phase 5).

normals.note: Outward normal of each sensor, devicetree faces 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, in body axes (scalar/sensors/veml6031.py lines 54-60: which side face is which is unknown, notes section 9). Replaced by the rotary-stage sweep (phase 5).

gains.note: Relative gain of each sensor, faces 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7: unit gains, as VEML6031Array takes them from the ideal cube (scalar/sensors/veml6031.py lines 18-20, which give the datasheet output tolerance as +-10 %). Replaced by the rotary-stage test (response of each sensor face-on).

dark_offset.note: Dark output, typical: scalar/sensors/veml6031.py line 47 (datasheet p.2).

noise.note: Noise per sample, 1 sigma, as a fraction of the face-on full-sun reading: scalar/sensors/sun_sensor.py line 72, carried into the VEML model (scalar/sensors/veml6031.py lines 17-19). Replaced by the rotary-stage test (spread of repeated readings).

mounting_tilt_sigma.note: 1-sigma mounting tilt of each normal, used only by the cube_tilt layout of scripts/sun_realism.py (was ASSUMED_TILT_DEG; 2.0 is the default tilt_deg of sun_mlp.flight_like_sensor). Not applied to the as-built rows, which fly the normals entry. Replaced by measured normals.

mounting_tilt_seed.note: Random seed that draws the cube_tilt layout of scripts/sun_realism.py (was ASSUMED_TILT_SEED). Not applied to the as-built rows. Not a hardware number; drops out once the normals are measured.

swing_amplitude.note: Half the peak-to-peak board temperature swing, one sinusoid per orbit, seen by gyro and magnetometer alike (scripts/mag_realism.py, was ASSUMED_TEMP_AMP_K). Replaced by a TMP112 log over an orbit: put its path in log_csv and set this and swing_phase to null.

swing_phase.note: Phase of the swing at t = 0; 0 = at its mean, warming (scripts/mag_realism.py, was ASSUMED_TEMP_PHASE_DEG).

log_csv.note: Path (from the repository root) of a logged board temperature: CSV with a header row and two columns, time [s] and temperature [deg C]. Replaces the swing (set swing_amplitude and swing_phase to null). Replayed end to end, repeating; the log's mean is taken as the temperature at which the biases above hold.

dipole_per_amp.note: Dipole per amp, column j = channel j. Computed from the S3 coil geometry (turns x area, air core) in scalar/sysid/magnetorquer_id.py lines 164-178; no source confirms the coil set (docs/LIMITATIONS.md, decisions not yet made). Replaced by a coil measurement (or the in-flight burst identification, notes section 3).

max_current.note: Full-scale current per channel: 3.3 V over 2 x 13 ohm, 2 x 13 ohm, 150.7 ohm (scalar/sysid/magnetorquer_id.py line 177). Replaced by measured coil resistance and driver output voltage.

inertia.note: 1.3 kg uniform 10 cm cube with axis factors 0.9, 1.0, 1.15 (scalar/dynamics.py line 49). Replaced by a CAD mass model or a pendulum measurement of the flight unit.

residual_dipole.note: Residual magnetic dipole of the spacecraft, coils off (scalar/control/rl_tune.py line 74). Replaced by a magnetic-cleanliness measurement of the assembled unit.

altitude.note: Circular orbit altitude: ScenarioSpec default (scalar/harness/spec.py line 42) and CircularOrbit default (scalar/environment/orbit.py line 49), whose docstring (line 3) calls 550 km a design point chosen to stress eclipse, not SCALAR's orbit. Replaced by the orbit the launch provides. Applied to the as-built rows only.

inclination.note: Orbit inclination of every closed-loop run: scalar/harness/spec.py line 43 and scalar/control/rl_tune.py line 72; scripts/absolute_without_gps.py line 30 calls it S7's orbit. The open-loop runs and the CircularOrbit default use 51.6 deg (scalar/environment/orbit.py line 50). Replaced by the orbit the launch provides. Applied to the as-built rows only.

raan.note: Right ascension of the ascending node at the start date (scalar/harness/spec.py line 44); no source. With epoch it sets where the Sun sits relative to the orbit plane, and so the eclipse share of each orbit. Replaced by the orbit the launch provides. Applied to the as-built rows only.

epoch.note: Start date and time of a run (scalar/harness/spec.py line 41, scalar/control/rl_tune.py line 73); no source. Sets the Sun direction and Earth's rotation at the start. Replaced by a planned operations date once launch is known. Applied to the as-built rows only.
